bmt-2025-geometry-tiebreaker-03.title: Power of a point twice
bmt-2025-geometry-tiebreaker-03.body:
Let $Z$ be the midpoint of $AM$, so $AZ=ZM=20$ and $ZD=30$. Power of $M$: $BM\cdot MC=AM\cdot MD=400$, and $BM=MC$, so $BM=MC=20$.

Power of $Z$: $BZ\cdot ZX=AZ\cdot ZD=600$ with $BZ+ZX=BX=50$, so $\{BZ,ZX\}=\{20,30\}$. Since $AB<AC$, $\angle ZMB$ is acute, which forces $BZ<20\sqrt2<30$, so $BZ=20$.

Then $MB=MZ=MC=20$, so $M$ is the circumcenter of $\triangle BZC$ and $\angle BZC=90^\circ$ (it subtends diameter $BC$). So $ZC=\sqrt{40^2-20^2}=20\sqrt3$. Power of $Z$ again: $ZY=\frac{600}{ZC}=10\sqrt3$. Hence $CY=ZC+ZY=30\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $30\sqrt3$**
